outlook: At midday Friday (about 10:30 a.m. CT), December corn was down 2¾ cents at $4.48½ and December Chicago wheat was off 3¼ cents at $6.00½, as funds kept selling ahead of the weekend and month-end with harvest moving quickly. January soybeans were up 2¼ cents at $12.37 and January canola gained C$4.40 to C$787.50, lifted by firmer vegetable oils as crude oil rose on reports of possible renewed U.S.–Iran fighting. December Minneapolis spring wheat slipped 2½ cents to $6.22 after Thursday's gains on China's inquiry for U.S. wheat. Prices are midday levels, not final closes; canola now tracks January, and cash bids are from Thursday's USDA Minneapolis report.
